attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation still assumes that the boundary anomaly admits the clean finite decomposition N=B\circ M+A with diagonal trace continuity and either positive A or no A. The hard Yang-Mills gap is to derive B_{12} and N_{12} from the actual reflected Wilson OPE/RG construction for a concrete locked pair, rather than postulating them as finite matrices.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity: for every collar width \delta and cutoff pair (a,L), the finite OS matrix N_{a,L,\delta,ij}=S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta) is positive semidefinite.
Use the closed-cone passage only for the actually controlled reflected probes to obtain N\succeq0 in the collar limit; this step is valid but only proves positivity for the collar-limit matrix N.
Model the remaining boundary collapse by N=B\circ M+A, where M is the intended same-theory zero-collar OS matrix, B is a normalized multiplicative hairpin factor, and A is an additive contact.
Apply the positive-contact elimination lemma: if A\succeq0 and diagonal trace continuity gives A_{11}=A_{22}=0, then A=0 on this two-observable sector.
The two-by-two OS condition for M is det M=N_{11}N_{22}-|N_{12}|^2/|B_{12}|^2\ge0, equivalently |N_{12}|^2\le |B_{12}|^2N_{11}N_{22}.
Thus nonrank-one boundary covariance is not automatically fatal; it becomes a falsifier only when a realized locked Wilson pair has collar correlation exceeding the boundary damping threshold.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It proves a valid finite-dimensional transfer criterion, not the analytic estimates required for Yang-Mills existence. We still lack a theorem that the RG cutoff-removal topology controls the relevant hairpin Wilson products, that the boundary OPE produces a normalized multiplicative B, and that the locked Wilson core is rich enough to test all dangerous boundary covariances.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Realized Boundary-Damping Detector

assumptions: The cutoff Schwinger forms are reflection-positive on the positive-time gauge-invariant test algebra for each regulator pair (a,L).
For the chosen collar Wilson observables, all reflected finite matrix entries converge in the RG cutoff-removal topology and then in the collar topology.
The multiplicative boundary anomaly is entrywise nonzero on the tested pair and normalized by diagonal trace continuity, so B_{11}=B_{22}=1 and N_{ii}=M_{ii}.
The intended zero-collar matrix is obtained by the Hadamard quotient M=B^{[-1]}\circ N rather than by changing the observable algebra.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive gauge-invariant Wilson collar Schwinger forms S_{a,L} restricted to a fixed locked two-observable core, with the limits a\downarrow0, L\uparrow\infty, and collar width \delta\downarrow0 taken only through reflected OS matrix entries.
target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions on the intended zero-collar gauge-invariant Wilson algebra, not on a boundary-renormalized enlargement or quotient.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated by convergence of every finite reflected matrix entry and by an explicit boundary anomaly relation N=B\circ M.

same-theory condition: the map F_i^\delta\mapsto F_i is fixed before taking the collar limit, and every boundary factor B_{ij} is either already part of the locked observable normalization or must pass the realized determinant test without adding new boundary degrees of freedom.

equations.label: collar positivity
equations.valid_when: The RG topology controls the reflected collar probes and the positivity cone is closed for these finite OS matrices.

equations.label: boundary anomaly relation
equations.valid_when: Collar collapse produces only a normalized multiplicative reflected Wilson hairpin factor, with no surviving additive contact term.

equations.label: same-theory determinant criterion
equations.valid_when: The two diagonal entries are finite and positive, diagonal trace continuity holds, and M=B^{[-1]}\circ N is the intended target OS matrix.

equations.label: realized falsifier inequality
equations.valid_when: The observed collar correlation coefficient exceeds the boundary damping supplied by the hairpin Gram factor.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find two locked Wilson collar observables for which the boundary OPE gives |B_{12}|<1 while the realized reflected collar correlation satisfies |N_{12}|/(N_{11}N_{22})^{1/2}>|B_{12}|; this produces a negative determinant in the target matrix.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the previous rich-cone caveat into a minimal realized-sector bridge: it neither assumes arbitrary positive matrices are realizable nor dismisses nonrank-one boundary covariance. It gives the exact two-observable condition under which collar OS positivity transfers to the intended same-theory OS matrix.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let a locked pair of gauge-invariant collar Wilson observables F_1^\delta,F_2^\delta have a reflected collar OS matrix N=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\lim_{a,L} S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\ge0. Suppose the intended same-theory boundary value M is related to the collar limit by a normalized multiplicative hairpin boundary Gram factor B with N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}, B_{ii}=1, and 0<|B_{12}|\le1. Then the same-theory OS passage is valid for this two-dimensional realized sector if and only if |N_{12}|^2\le |B_{12}|^2N_{11}N_{22}. Hence a realized pair with |N_{12}|^2>|B_{12}|^2N_{11}N_{22} is a concrete falsifier of the bridge, while a nonrank-one B is harmless on this sector whenever the realized collar correlation is below the boundary damping threshold.

assumptions: The additive contact matrix A is positive semidefinite, not merely Hermitian.
Each diagonal additive defect vanishes after the locked observable normalization is fixed.
The finite core is closed under the reflected pairings used in the OS quadratic form.
definitions: Finite core means a finite list of locked gauge-invariant observables whose reflected OS matrix entries are all controlled by the cutoff-removal topology.
Diagonal trace continuity means the self-pairing of each collar observable converges to the self-pairing of its intended zero-collar observable without an extra boundary term.
A positive additive contact is a positive semidefinite matrix added to reflected OS pairings by boundary collapse.
A multiplicative damping factor is a normalized entrywise factor B_{ij} multiplying the intended matrix M before the collar limit is observed as N.

equations.label: zero diagonal kills positive contact
equations.valid_when: A is a finite positive semidefinite additive contact matrix.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit a boundary contact term whose diagonal defects vanish but whose off-diagonal entries do not; if the contact is positive this is impossible, so such an example would show the contact is indefinite or that diagonal trace continuity was not actually valid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This removes one false obstruction from the bridge and focuses the remaining analytic work on multiplicative reflected Wilson hairpin factors or on contacts that fail positivity.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the collar-to-boundary defect decomposes as N=B\circ M+A with A\succeq0 and diagonal trace continuity gives A_{ii}=0 on the tested finite core, then A=0 on that core. Therefore a positive additive boundary contact cannot be the remaining obstruction once diagonal traces are valid; the obstruction must be multiplicative damping or an indefinite/pair-dependent contact.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this bridge if the RG construction cannot even define mixed reflected Wilson collar entries N_{12}, or if the target algebra must be changed to absorb B as a boundary sector.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the lemma if one can prove for a dense locked Wilson core that every boundary factor satisfies either B_{12}=1 or the realized correlations obey |N_{12}|^2\le |B_{12}|^2N_{11}N_{22}, with the same-theory observable identification fixed.
control_decision.reason: The branch made substantive progress by replacing the vague rich-cone requirement with a valid realized determinant threshold. The next work should compute or bound the two quantities in that threshold for actual reflected Wilson hairpin probes.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge now has a finite realized-sector clause: after closed-cone positivity gives N\succeq0, same-theory positivity for M requires a determinant threshold whenever a multiplicative boundary factor B is present.

The locked Wilson core must be assessed by realized correlation strength, not by an abstract rich-cone assumption. The algebra is adequate only if it can either force \rho_N\le |B_{12}| for all pairs or expose a determinant falsifier.
The required topology must control mixed reflected Wilson collar products, especially the entries N_{12}; controlling only one-point or diagonal limits is insufficient.

falsifiers: Concrete determinant falsifier: a locked pair with |N_{12}|/(N_{11}N_{22})^{1/2}>|B_{12}| gives det M<0, so collar positivity does not imply same-theory OS positivity.

Boundary-decomposition falsifier: the collar collapse produces an additive contact with zero diagonal but nonzero off-diagonal, showing either positivity of the contact or diagonal trace continuity has failed.
Topology falsifier: the multiscale convergence controls individual Wilson loop expectations but not the mixed reflected products needed to define N_{12}.
Same-theory falsifier: the only way to restore positivity is to absorb B into a new boundary Hilbert sector or boundary counterterm not present in the locked gauge-invariant algebra.

Richness falsifier: every realizable locked Wilson pair has \rho_N\le |B_{12}| even when B is nonrank-one, so the proposed determinant test cannot detect the boundary covariance on the available algebra.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 196 clarifies that the boundary Gram obstruction is a threshold phenomenon, not a yes/no property of B alone. The closed-cone argument is valid for the collar-limit OS matrix N, and positive additive contacts vanish once diagonal trace continuity is valid. The remaining same-theory question is whether the intended target matrix M=B^{[-1]}\circ N stays positive on realized Wilson sectors. For two observables this is exactly the inequality \rho_N\le |B_{12}|. This avoids the earlier overclaim that every nonrank-one boundary Gram factor is automatically fatal, while still giving a concrete falsifier: a realized collar correlation larger than the hairpin damping produces a negative OS determinant.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Pick a minimal pair of reflected Wilson hairpin observables sharing a boundary footprint. Compute the leading boundary OPE contribution to B_{12}, normalize B_{ii}=1, and compare it with a rigorous or perturbative bound on the realized collar correlation coefficient \rho_N=|N_{12}|/(N_{11}N_{22})^{1/2}; the first target is to decide whether \rho_N>|B_{12}| can occur.
